t2087_text: 從此西北行二千餘里，至摩臘婆國（即南羅國。南印度境）。摩臘婆國，周六千餘里。國大都城周三十餘里，據莫醯河東南。土地膏腴，稼穡殷盛，草木榮茂，花菓繁實，特宜宿麥，多食餅麨。人性善順，大抵聰敏，言辭雅亮，學藝優深。五印度境，兩國重學，西南摩臘婆國，東北摩揭陀國，貴德尚仁，明敏強學。而此國也，邪正雜信。伽藍數百所，僧徒二萬餘人，習學小乘正量部法。天祠數百，異道寔眾，多是塗灰之侶也。國志曰：六十年前，王號尸羅阿迭多（唐言戒日）。機慧高明，才學贍敏，愛育四生，敬崇三寶。始自誕靈，洎乎沒齒，貌無瞋色，手不害生。象馬飲水，漉而後𩚅，恐傷水性也。其仁慈如此。在位五十餘年，野獸狎人，舉國黎庶咸不殺害。居宮之側建立精舍，窮諸工巧，備盡莊嚴，中作七佛世尊之像。每歲恒設無遮大會，招集四方僧徒，修施四事供養，或以三衣道具，或以七寶珍奇。奕世相承，美業無替。
translation: From here, traveling northwest for more than two thousand li, one reaches the country of Mālava (摩臘婆國) (that is, the country of Southern Lāṭa (南羅); within the borders of South India). The country of Mālava is more than six thousand li in circumference. The capital city is more than thirty li in circumference and is situated to the southeast of the Mahī River. The land is fertile, agriculture is flourishing, the vegetation is lush, and flowers and fruits are abundant. It is particularly suitable for winter wheat, and the people eat mostly cakes and parched grain. The nature of the people is gentle and compliant; they are generally intelligent, their speech is elegant and clear, and their learning and arts are profound. Within the borders of the Five Indias, two countries place great importance on learning: the country of Mālava in the southwest and the country of Magadha (摩揭陀國) in the northeast; they value virtue, honor benevolence, and are brilliant and diligent in their studies. However, in this country, both heterodox and orthodox beliefs are practiced. There are several hundred saṃghārāmas with more than twenty thousand monks, who study the teachings of the Sammatiya school of the Lesser Vehicle. There are several hundred deva temples, and the number of heterodox practitioners is substantial; most of them are followers who smear themselves with ashes. The local records state: sixty years ago, there was a king named Śīlāditya (in Chinese, "Sun of Virtue" (戒日)). His ingenuity and wisdom were brilliant, his talent and learning were vast and sharp, he cherished and nurtured the four types of living beings, and he revered and honored the Three Jewels. From his birth until his death, his countenance never showed anger, and his hands never harmed a living creature. When his elephants and horses drank water, he would have it filtered first, fearing that he might injure the life-force of the water. His benevolence was such as this. During his reign of more than fifty years, wild beasts became familiar with humans, and the people of the entire country refrained from killing. Beside the palace, he built a *vihāra* (精舍) with the utmost craftsmanship and exquisite adornment, and within it were fashioned images of the seven World-Honored Buddhas. Every year, he regularly held a great unrestricted assembly (無遮大會, *mokṣa-mahāpariṣad*), gathering monks from all directions to provide them with the four monastic requisites, whether in the form of the three robes and religious implements, or various rare treasures of the seven precious gems. This tradition has been passed down through successive generations, and this noble practice has never ceased.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 大城西北二十餘里，至婆羅門邑，傍有陷坑，秋夏淫滯，彌淹旬日，雖納眾流，而無積水。其傍又建小窣堵波。聞諸先志曰：昔者大慢婆羅門生身陷入地獄之處。昔此邑中，有婆羅門，生知博物，學冠時彥；內外典籍，究極幽微，曆數玄文，若視諸掌；風範清高，令問遐被。王甚珍敬，國人宗重。門人千數，味道欽風。每而言曰：「吾為世出，述聖導凡，先賢後哲，無與我比。彼大自在天、婆藪天、那羅延天、佛世尊者，人皆風靡，祖述其道，莫不圖形，競修祇敬。我今德踰於彼，名擅於時，不有所異，其何以顯？」遂用赤栴檀刻作大自在天、婆藪天、那羅延天、佛世尊等像。為座四足，凡有所至，負以自隨，其慢傲也如此。時西印度有苾芻跋陀羅縷支（唐言賢愛），妙極因明，深窮異論，道風淳粹，戒香郁烈，少欲知足，無求於物，聞而歎曰：「惜哉！時無人矣。令彼愚夫，敢行兇德。」於是荷錫遠遊，來至此國，以其宿心，具白於王。王見弊服，心未之敬，然高其志，強為之禮。遂設論座，告婆羅門曰。婆羅門聞而笑曰：「彼何人斯，敢懷此志？」命其徒屬，來就論場，數百千眾，前後侍聽。賢愛服弊故衣，敷草而坐。彼婆羅門踞所持座，非斥正法，敷述邪宗。苾芻清辯若流，循環往復。婆羅門久而謝屈。王乃謂曰：「久濫虛名，罔上惑眾，先典有記，論負當戮。」欲以鑪鐵，令其坐上。婆羅門窘迫，乃歸命求救。賢愛愍之，乃請王曰：「大王仁禮遠洽，頌聲載途，當布慈育，勿行殘酷，恕其不逮，唯所去就。」王令乘驢，巡告城邑。婆羅門恥其戮辱，發憤歐血。苾芻聞已，往慰之曰：「爾學苞內外，聲聞遐邇，榮辱之事，進退當明。夫名者，何實乎？」婆羅門憤恚，深詈苾芻，謗毀大乘，輕蔑先聖。言聲未靜，地便拆裂，生身墜陷，遺迹斯在。
translation: More than twenty *li* northwest of the great city, one arrives at the Brahmin village (Brāhmaṇagrāma). Nearby is a deep pit; during the autumn and summer, despite heavy and persistent rains that last for ten days, and although it receives many streams, the water never accumulates. Beside it, a small stūpa has been built. According to ancient records, this is the place where a highly arrogant Brahmin fell into hell while still alive. Formerly, in this village, there was a Brahmin who was naturally wise and widely learned, his scholarship surpassing that of the eminent men of his time. He had thoroughly investigated the profound mysteries of both internal and external scriptures, and the abstruse texts of astronomy and mathematics were as clear to him as if he were looking at the palm of his own hand. His character was noble and refined, and his reputation spread far and wide. The king held him in great esteem and respect, and the people of the country honored him. He had thousands of disciples who admired his way and were drawn to his influence. He would often say, "I have appeared in this world to expound the sacred and guide the ordinary; neither the sages of the past nor the philosophers of the future can compare to me. People are all swept up in following Maheśvara, Vāsudeva, Nārāyaṇa, and the World-Honored Buddha; they propagate their doctrines, paint their images, and vie with one another to offer them worship. Now, since my virtue exceeds theirs and my fame dominates the age, if I do not do something different, how can I manifest my greatness?" He then used red sandalwood to carve images of Maheśvara, Vāsudeva, Nārāyaṇa, and the World-Honored Buddha. He made them the four legs of his seat, and wherever he went, he carried it with him. Such was his arrogance. At that time, in Western India, there was a bhikṣu named Bhadraruci (in Chinese, "Virtuous Love" [賢愛]), who had attained the pinnacle of *hetuvidyā* (logic) and had deeply exhausted the study of heterodox doctrines. His moral conduct was pure and refined, the fragrance of his precepts was intense, and he was possessed of few desires and contentment, seeking nothing from the world. Upon hearing of this, he sighed and said, "Alas! The times are devoid of men, allowing that foolish fellow to dare to practice such wicked deeds." Thereupon, he shouldered his khakkhara (monk's staff) and traveled from afar, arriving in this country, where he fully explained his long-held intention to the king. When the king saw his tattered robes, he did not feel much respect in his heart, yet he esteemed his ambition and reluctantly accorded him the proper courtesies. He then set up a debate seat and informed the Brahmin. The Brahmin heard this and laughed, saying, "Who is that person, that he dares to harbor such an ambition?" He ordered his followers to come to the debate arena, and hundreds of thousands of people gathered before and behind to listen. Bhadraruci wore his tattered, old robes and spread out grass to sit upon. The Brahmin sat perched upon the seat he had brought, denouncing the true Dharma and expounding his heterodox doctrines. The bhikṣu’s clear eloquence flowed like a stream, circling back and forth in argument. After a long time, the Brahmin admitted defeat. The king then said to him, "You have long abused a false reputation, deceiving your superiors and confusing the masses. The ancient codes record that one who loses a debate must be executed." He intended to use a red-hot iron seat to make him sit upon it. The Brahmin, in dire straits, surrendered and begged for his life. Bhadraruci took pity on him and petitioned the king, saying, "Great King, your benevolence and propriety are known far and wide, and your praises fill the roads; you should spread compassionate nurturance rather than practicing cruelty. Forgive his inadequacies and let him go as he pleases." The king ordered him to ride a donkey and announce his defeat throughout the city and its suburbs. The Brahmin, ashamed of this humiliation, became enraged and vomited blood. Upon hearing of this, the bhikṣu went to comfort him, saying, "Your learning encompasses both internal and external doctrines, and your reputation is known far and wide; you should clearly understand the nature of honor and disgrace, and when to advance or retreat. As for fame, what reality does it possess?" The Brahmin, filled with resentment, bitterly reviled the bhikṣu, slandered the Mahāyāna, and spoke with contempt of the ancient sages. Before his words had even died away, the earth split asunder, and he fell alive into the pit; the traces of this event still remain.

t2087_text: 自此西南入海交，西北行二千四五百里，至阿吒釐國（南印度境）。阿吒釐國，周六千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛，珍寶盈積，稼穡雖備，興販為業。土地沙鹵，花菓稀少。出胡椒樹，樹葉若蜀椒也。出薰陸香樹，樹葉若棠梨也。氣序熱，多風埃。人性澆薄，貴財賤德。文字語言，儀形法則，大同摩臘婆國。多不信福，縱有信者，宗事天神。祠館十餘所，異道雜居。
translation: From here, traveling southwest into a maritime bay and then northwest for two thousand four or five hundred *li*, one reaches the country of Aṭali (阿吒釐國) (within the borders of South India). The country of Aṭali is more than six thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than twenty *li* in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous, and precious treasures are accumulated in abundance. Although agriculture is practiced, the people make their living through trade. The land is sandy and saline, and flowers and fruits are scarce. It produces the black pepper tree, the leaves of which resemble those of the Sichuan pepper. It also produces the frankincense tree, the leaves of which resemble those of the flowering pear. The climate is hot, and there is much wind and dust. The nature of the people is shallow and fickle; they value wealth and despise virtue. Their script, language, customs, and laws are largely the same as those of the country of Mālava (摩臘婆國). Most do not believe in merit, and even among those who do, they revere and serve the heavenly deities. There are more than ten temples, where various heterodox sects dwell together.

translation: Traveling northwest from the country of Mālava (摩臘婆國) for three days, one reaches the country of Kaṭṭa (契吒國) (within the borders of South India). The country of Kaṭṭa is more than three thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city is over twenty *li* in circuit. The population is dense, and the households are wealthy. There is no great sovereign; it is subject to the country of Mālava, and its climate, products, and customs are consequently the same as that country. There are more than ten monasteries and over one thousand monks, who study both the Great and Small Vehicles with equal diligence. There are several dozen *deva* temples, and the non-Buddhists are numerous.

t2087_text: 從此北行千餘里，至伐臘毘國（即比羅羅國。南印度境）。伐臘毘國，周六千餘里。國大都城周三十餘里。土地所產，氣序所宜，風俗人性，同摩臘婆國。居人殷盛，家室富饒，積財百億者乃有百餘室矣。遠方奇貨，多聚其國。伽藍百餘所，僧徒六千餘人，多學小乘正量部法。天祠數百，異道寔多。如來在世，屢遊此國，故無憂王於佛所止，皆樹旌表，建窣堵波。過去三佛坐及經行說法之處，遺迹相間。今王，剎帝利種也，即昔摩臘婆國尸羅阿迭多王之姪，今羯若鞠闍國尸羅阿迭多王之子婿，號杜魯婆跋吒（唐言常叡）。情性躁急，智謀淺近。然而淳信三寶，歲設大會七日，以殊珍上味，供養僧眾。三衣醫藥之價，七寶奇貴之珍，既以總施，倍價酬贖。貴德尚賢，遵道重學，遠方高僧，特加禮敬。去城不遠，有大伽藍，阿折羅阿羅漢之所建立，德慧、堅慧菩薩之所遊止，於中制論，竝盛流布。
translation: From here, traveling north for more than one thousand *li*, one arrives at the country of Valabhī (伐臘毘國) (also called the country of Bīlala; it is within the borders of Southern India). The country of Valabhī is more than six thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city is more than thirty *li* in circuit. The produce of the land, the suitability of the climate, and the customs and human nature of the people are the same as in the country of Mālava (摩臘婆國). The inhabitants are prosperous, and the households are wealthy; there are more than one hundred families who have accumulated wealth of a hundred *koṭi*s. Rare goods from distant regions are mostly gathered in this country. There are more than one hundred *saṃghārāma*s, with more than six thousand monks, who mostly study the teachings of the Hīnayāna Saṃmitīya school. There are several hundred *deva* temples, and the heterodox sects are very numerous. When the Tathāgata was in the world, he frequently traveled to this country; therefore, King Aśoka erected markers and built *stūpa*s at all the places where the Buddha stopped. The sites where the three past Buddhas sat, walked, and preached the Dharma are interspersed among them. The current king is of the Kṣatriya caste; he is the nephew of the former King Śīlāditya of the country of Mālava and the son-in-law of the current King Śīlāditya of the country of Kanyākubja (羯若鞠闍國). His name is Dhruvabhaṭa (杜魯婆跋吒) (in the language of Tang, this means "Permanently Intelligent"). His temperament is impetuous, and his wisdom and strategy are shallow. However, he has pure faith in the Three Jewels. Every year, he holds a great assembly for seven days, offering rare treasures and superior delicacies to the community of monks. He gives away the value of the three robes and medicines, as well as rare and precious treasures of the seven kinds, and then redeems them at double their price. He values virtue and honors the worthy; he follows the Way and respects learning. He shows special reverence and respect to high-ranking monks from distant regions. Not far from the city is a great monastery (saṃghārāma) established by the Arhat Ācāra, where the Bodhisattvas Guṇamati and Sthiramati resided and composed treatises that are widely circulated.

translation: From here, traveling northwest for over seven hundred li, one reaches the country of Ānandapura (in the territory of Western India). The country of Ānandapura is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circuit. The population is dense and the households are wealthy. There is no great sovereign, and it is subject to the country of Mālava. The soil, climate, and the rules of writing are also the same as there. There are more than ten sanghārāmas, with fewer than one thousand monks, who study the teachings of the Sāmmitīya school of the Lesser Vehicle. There are several dozen deva temples, where followers of various paths live together.

translation: Traveling westward from the kingdom of Valabhī (伐臘毘國) for over five hundred li, one reaches the kingdom of Suraṭṭha (蘇剌侘國) (in the territory of Western India). The kingdom of Suraṭṭha is over four thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the kingdom is over thirty li in circuit and borders the Mahī River (莫醯河) to the west. The inhabitants are numerous and their households are wealthy. It is subject to the kingdom of Valabhī. The land is saline and alkaline, and flowers and fruits are scarce. Although the cold and heat are balanced, the wind blows incessantly. The local customs are shallow and the people’s temperament is impulsive. They do not care for learning arts, and they believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are over fifty saṃghārāmas (伽藍) with more than three thousand monks, who mostly study the teachings of the Mahāyāna Sthavira school. There are over one hundred deva temples, where various non-Buddhist sects dwell together. As the country lies on the route to the Western Sea, the people all rely on the benefits of the sea, engaging in trade as their profession and exchanging goods to supply what is lacking.

t2087_text: 從伐臘毘國北行千八百餘里，至瞿折羅國（西印度境）。瞿折羅國，周五千餘里。國大都城號毘羅摩羅，周三十餘里。土宜風俗，同蘇剌侘國。居人殷盛，家產富饒。多事外道，少信佛法。伽藍一所，僧百餘人，習學小乘教說一切有部。天祠數十，異道雜居。王，剎帝利種也，年在弱冠，智勇高遠，深信佛法，高尚異能。
translation: Traveling north from the country of Valabhī (伐臘毘國) for more than 1,800 li, one reaches the country of Gūrjara (瞿折羅國) (in the region of Western India). The country of Gūrjara is more than 5,000 li in circuit. The capital city is named Bhīlamāla (毘羅摩羅), and it is more than 30 li in circuit. The soil, climate, and customs are the same as those of the country of Surāṣṭra (蘇剌侘國). The inhabitants are prosperous, and their households are wealthy. They mostly serve non-Buddhist paths and have little faith in the Buddha’s teachings. There is one monastery with more than 100 monks, who study the teachings of the Small Vehicle (Hīnayāna) according to the Sarvāstivāda school. There are several dozen Deva temples where followers of various non-Buddhist paths live together. The king is of the Kṣatriya caste; he is in the prime of his youth, his wisdom and courage are far-reaching, he deeply believes in the Buddha’s teachings, and he holds noble and extraordinary talents in high regard.

translation: Traveling southeast from here for over 2,800 li, one reaches the country of Ujjayanī (鄔闍衍那國) (in the territory of South India). The country of Ujjayanī is over 6,000 li in circuit. The capital city is over 30 li in circuit. The soil, climate, and customs are the same as those of the country of Surāṣṭra (蘇剌侘國). The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous, and the families are wealthy. There are several dozen saṃghārāmas, most of which are dilapidated, with only three or five remaining in use. There are over 300 monks, who study both the Great and Lesser Vehicles. There are several dozen Deva temples, where followers of various heterodox paths live together. The king is of the Brāhmaṇa caste; he is widely read in heterodox texts and does not believe in the true Dharma. Not far from the city is a stūpa, which is the site where King Aśoka created a hell.

t2087_text: 從此東北行千餘里，至擲枳陀國（南印度境）。擲枳陀國，周四千餘里。國大都城周十五六里。土稱沃壤，稼穡滋植，宜菽、麥，多華菓。氣序調暢，人性善順。多信外道，少敬佛法。伽藍數十，少有僧徒。天祠十餘所，外道千餘人。王，婆羅門種也，篤信三寶，尊重有德，諸方博達之士，多集此國。
translation: Traveling northeast from here for more than a thousand *li*, one arrives at the country of Zhizhituo (擲枳陀國) (within the borders of South India). The country of Zhizhituo is more than four thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city of the country is fifteen or sixteen *li* in circuit. The soil is described as fertile, and the crops are abundant; it is suitable for beans and wheat, and there are many flowers and fruits. The climate is temperate and pleasant, and the people are gentle and compliant by nature. They mostly believe in non-Buddhist paths and have little respect for the Buddhadharma. There are several dozen *saṃghārāmas* (monasteries), but few monks. There are more than ten *deva* temples, and over a thousand followers of non-Buddhist paths. The king is of the Brahmin caste; he is a devout believer in the Three Jewels and holds virtuous people in high esteem, so many learned scholars from various regions gather in this country.

t2087_text: 從此北行九百餘里，至摩醯濕伐羅補羅國（中印度境）。摩醯濕伐羅補羅國，周三千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。土宜風俗，同鄔闍衍那國。宗敬外道，不信佛法。天祠數十，多是塗灰之侶。王，婆羅門種也。不甚敬信佛法。
translation: From here, traveling northward for more than nine hundred li, one reaches the country of Maheśvarapura (in the region of Central India). The country of Maheśvarapura is more than three thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than twenty li in circuit. The soil, products, and customs are the same as those of the country of Ujjayanī (鄔闍衍那國). They revere and honor non-Buddhist paths and do not believe in the Buddha-Dharma. There are several dozen Deva temples, most of them belonging to followers who smear themselves with ash. The king is of the Brahmin caste and does not have much faith or respect for the Buddha-Dharma.

t2087_text: 從此還至瞿折羅國，復北行荒野險磧，經千九百餘里，渡信度大河，至信度國（西印度境）。信度國，周七千餘里。國大都城號毘苫婆補羅，周三十餘里。宜穀稼，豐宿麥，出金、銀、鍮石，宜牛、羊、橐駝、騾畜之屬。橐駝卑小，唯有一峯。多出赤鹽，色如赤石，白鹽、黑鹽及白石鹽等，異域遠方以之為藥。人性剛烈而質直，數鬪諍，多誹讟。學不好博，深信佛法。伽藍數百所，僧徒萬餘人，竝學小乘正量部法，大抵懈怠，性行弊穢；其有精勤賢善之徒，獨處閑寂，遠迹山林，夙夜匪懈，多證聖果。天祠三十餘所，異道雜居。王，戍陀羅種也，性淳質，敬佛法。如來在昔頗遊此國，故無憂王於聖迹處建窣堵波數十所。烏波毱多大阿羅漢屢遊此國，演法開導，所止之處，皆旌遺迹，或建僧伽藍，或樹窣堵波，往往間起，可略而言。信度河側千餘里陂澤間，有數百千戶，於此宅居，其性剛烈，唯殺是務。牧牛自活，無所係命。若男若女，無貴無賤，剃鬚髮，服袈裟，像類苾芻，而行俗事，專執小見，非斥大乘。聞諸先志曰：昔此地民庶安忍，但事凶殘。時有羅漢愍其顛墜，為化彼故，乘虛而來，現大神通，示希有事，令眾信受，漸導言教。諸人敬悅，願奉指誨。羅漢知眾心順，為授三歸，息其兇暴，悉斷生殺，剃髮染衣，恭行法教。年代浸遠，世易時移，守善既虧，餘風不殄，雖服法衣，嘗無戒善。子孫奕世，習以成俗。
translation: From here I returned to the country of Gurjara (瞿折羅國), then traveled north through wild wastes and dangerous deserts for over one thousand nine hundred li, crossed the great Sindhu (信度) River, and arrived at the country of Sindhu (in the territory of Western India). The country of Sindhu is over seven thousand li in circuit. The capital city is named Viṣambhapura (毘苫婆補羅), and it is over thirty li in circuit. The land is suitable for grain crops and is abundant in winter wheat; it produces gold, silver, and brass, and is suitable for raising cattle, sheep, camels, and mules. The camels are small and have only one hump. It produces much red salt, the color of which is like red stone, as well as white salt, black salt, and white rock salt; people in distant foreign lands use these as medicine. The people are fierce and straightforward by nature, frequently quarrel, and are prone to slander. They are not widely learned, but they deeply believe in the Buddhadharma. There are several hundred monasteries with over ten thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Sammitīya school of the Hīnayāna; for the most part, they are indolent, and their character and conduct are corrupt. However, those who are diligent, virtuous, and good dwell alone in quiet seclusion, withdrawing far into the mountains and forests, and, working day and night without slackening, many attain the holy fruits. There are over thirty Deva temples, where followers of different paths live together. The king is of the Śūdra caste; he is pure and simple by nature and respects the Buddhadharma. In the past, the Tathāgata traveled extensively in this country, and therefore King Aśoka built several dozen stūpas at the sites of the holy traces. The great arhat Upagupta (烏波毱多) frequently traveled to this country to preach the Dharma and provide guidance. At every place he stayed, he marked the sacred traces, either by building a monastery (saṃghārāma) or erecting a stūpa; these rise up here and there, and can be briefly described. Along the side of the Sindhu River (信度河), in the midst of marshes extending over a thousand li, there are several hundred thousand households residing there. Their nature is fierce and violent, and they are devoted solely to killing. They herd cattle to sustain their lives and have no other means of livelihood. Whether male or female, noble or base, they shave their hair and beards and wear the kaṣāya (monastic robes), appearing like bhikṣus while engaging in secular affairs; they stubbornly hold to narrow views and reject the Great Vehicle (Mahāyāna). I have heard from the records of the ancients: "In the past, the common people of this land were hardened and cruel, devoted only to violence." At that time, an arhat took pity on their fallen state and, in order to transform them, came through the void, manifesting great supernatural powers and displaying rare wonders, causing the multitude to believe and accept his teachings, which he introduced gradually. The people were respectful and pleased, and wished to follow his instructions. The arhat, knowing that the hearts of the multitude were compliant, administered the three refuges to them, calmed their ferocity, caused them to completely cease killing, and had them shave their hair, dye their garments, and respectfully practice the teachings of the Dharma. As the ages grew distant and the world changed with the passage of time, their adherence to goodness faltered, yet the remnants of their old customs were not extinguished; although they wear the robes of the Dharma, they have never possessed the precepts or virtue. Their descendants, generation after generation, have made this their custom.

t2087_text: 從此東行九百餘里，渡信度河東岸，至茂羅三部盧國（西印度境）。茂羅三部盧國，周四千餘里。國大都城周三十餘里。居人殷盛，家室富饒。役屬磔迦國。土田良沃，氣序調順。風俗質直，好學尚德。多事天神，少信佛法。伽藍十餘所，多已圮壞，少有僧徒，學無專習。天祠八所，異道雜居。有日天祠，莊嚴甚麗，其日天像鑄以黃金，飾以奇寶。靈鑒幽通，神功潛被，女樂遞奏，明炬繼日，香花供養，初無廢絕。五印度國諸王豪族，莫不於此捨施珍寶，建立福舍，以飲食醫藥給濟貧病。諸國之人來此求願，常有千數，天祠四周，池沼花林，甚可遊賞。
translation: From here, traveling east for over nine hundred li and crossing to the eastern bank of the Indus River (Sindhu), one arrives at the country of Mūlasthānapura (茂羅三部盧國) (in the region of Western India). The country of Mūlasthānapura is over four thousand li in circuit. The capital city is over thirty li in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and the households are wealthy. It is subject to the country of Takka (磔迦國). The land is fertile and productive, and the climate is temperate and regular. The customs of the people are honest and straightforward; they are fond of learning and value virtue. They mostly serve the heavenly deities and have little faith in the Buddha-dharma. There are more than ten sanghārāmas, most of which are dilapidated; there are few monks, and they do not specialize in any particular study. There are eight deva temples where followers of various heterodox paths live together. There is a Temple of the Sun God, which is extremely magnificent and beautiful; the image of the Sun God is cast in gold and adorned with rare jewels. Its spiritual influence is profound and mysterious, and its divine efficacy is secretly bestowed. Female musicians play in rotation, bright torches burn continuously day and night, and offerings of incense and flowers are never interrupted. The kings and noble families of the five Indias never fail to donate precious treasures here and establish charitable houses to provide food, drink, and medicine to the poor and the sick. People from various countries come here to offer prayers, often numbering in the thousands. Around the deva temple, the ponds and flowery woods are most pleasant for sightseeing.

t2087_text: 從此東北行七百餘里，至鉢伐多國（北印度境）。鉢伐多國，周五千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛。役屬磔迦國。多早稻，宜宿、麥。氣序調適，風俗質直，人性躁急，言含鄙辭。學藝深博，邪正雜信。伽藍十餘所，僧徒千餘人。大小二乘，兼功習學。四窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。天祠二十，異道雜居。城側有大伽藍，僧徒百餘人，並學大乘教，即是昔慎那弗呾羅（唐言最勝子）論師於此製《瑜伽師地釋論》，亦是賢愛論師、德光論師本出家處。此大伽藍為天火所燒，摧殘荒圮。
translation: From here, traveling northeast for more than seven hundred li, one reaches the country of Parvata (鉢伐多國) (within the borders of Northern India). The country of Parvata is more than five thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than twenty li in circuit. The inhabitants are prosperous and numerous. It is subject to the country of Takka (磔迦國). There is much early-ripening rice, and it is suitable for winter wheat. The climate is temperate, the customs are simple and honest, the people’s temperament is impetuous and hasty, and their speech contains vulgar expressions. They are deeply learned in the arts and sciences, and they believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are more than ten monasteries with over a thousand monks, who study both the Mahayana and Hinayana teachings. There are four stūpas, which were built by King Aśoka. There are twenty Deva temples, where followers of various heterodox paths live together. Beside the city is a large monastery with over a hundred monks, all of whom study the Mahayana teachings; this is where the former śāstra master Jinaputra (in Chinese, "Most Victorious Son" (最勝子)) composed the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra-vyākhyā*, and it is also the place where the śāstra masters Bhadraruci and Guṇaprabha originally entered the monastic order. This large monastery was burned by celestial fire and is now ruined and desolate.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 從信度國西南行千五六百里，至阿點婆翅羅國（西印度境）。阿點婆翅羅國，周五千餘里。國大都城號朅䶩濕伐羅，周三十餘里。僻在西境，臨信度河，隣大海濱。屋宇莊嚴，多有珍寶。近無君長，統屬信度國。地下濕，土斥鹵，穢草荒茂，疇壟少墾，穀稼雖備，宿、麥特豐。氣序微寒，風飈勁烈。宜牛、羊、橐駝、騾畜之類。人性暴急，不好習學。語言微異中印度。其俗淳質，敬崇三寶。伽藍八十餘所，僧徒五千餘人，多學小乘正量部法。天祠十所，多是塗灰外道之所居止。城中有大自在天祠。祠宇彫飾，天像靈鑒，塗灰外道遊舍其中。在昔如來頗遊此國，說法度人，導凡利俗，故無憂王於聖迹處建六窣堵波焉。
translation: Traveling southwest from the country of Sindhu (信度國) for fifteen or sixteen hundred li, one reaches the country of Audumbatira (阿點婆翅羅國) (within the borders of West India). The country of Audumbatira is over five thousand li in circuit. The great capital city is named Khasvara (朅䶩濕伐羅), and it is over thirty li in circuit. It is situated in a remote western region, bordering the Sindhu River and adjacent to the shore of the great sea. The buildings are magnificent and contain many precious treasures. Recently, it has had no sovereign and is under the jurisdiction of the country of Sindhu. The ground is low and damp, the soil is saline, and foul weeds grow in abundance. The fields are little cultivated; although all types of grain are present, winter wheat is particularly abundant. The climate is slightly cold, and the winds are fierce and strong. It is suitable for cattle, sheep, camels, mules, and similar livestock. The people are impetuous and do not like to study. Their language differs slightly from that of Mid-India. Their customs are simple and honest, and they revere the Three Jewels. There are more than eighty saṃghārāmas and over five thousand monks, most of whom study the teachings of the Sāṃmitīya school of the Lesser Vehicle. There are ten deva temples, mostly inhabited by ash-smearing heterodox ascetics. In the city, there is a temple to Maheśvara (大自在天). The temple is carved and adorned, and the image of the deity is spiritually responsive; ash-smearing heterodox ascetics reside within it. In the past, the Tathāgata traveled extensively in this country, preaching the Dharma to save people and guiding the commoners to benefit the populace; therefore, King Aśoka (無憂王) built six stūpas at the sites of these sacred traces.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 從此西行，減二千里，至狼揭羅國（西印度境）。狼揭羅國，東西南北各數千里。國大都城周三十餘里，號窣菟黎濕伐羅。土地沃潤，稼穡滋盛。氣序風俗，同阿點婆翅羅國。居人殷盛，多諸珍寶。臨大海濱，入西女國之路也。無大君長，據川自立，不相承命，役屬波剌斯國。文字大同印度，語言少異。邪正兼信。伽藍百餘所，僧徒六千餘人，大小二乘，兼功習學。天祠數百所，塗灰外道，其徒極眾。城中有大自在天祠，莊嚴壯麗，塗灰外道之所宗事。
translation: Traveling west from here for less than two thousand li, one reaches the country of Laṅgala (狼揭羅國) (within the borders of Western India). The country of Laṅgala measures several thousand li in each of the four directions. The capital city is over thirty li in circumference and is named Sthūlīśvara (窣菟黎濕伐羅). The land is fertile and moist, and crops are abundant. The climate and customs are the same as those of the country of Audumbatira (阿點婆翅羅國). The inhabitants are prosperous and possess many precious treasures. It borders the great ocean and is the route to the country of the Western Women (西女國). There is no great monarch; the people occupy the river valleys and establish themselves independently, not acknowledging the authority of one another, and are subject to the country of Pārsi (波剌斯國). Their writing is largely the same as that of India, though their spoken language differs slightly. They believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are over one hundred monasteries with more than six thousand monks, who study and practice the teachings of both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna. There are several hundred Deva temples, and the ash-smearing heretics are extremely numerous. Inside the city is a temple of Maheśvara (大自在天), magnificent and grand, which is the place of worship for the ash-smearing heretics.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 自此西北，至波剌斯國（雖非印度之國，路次附見。舊曰波斯，略也）。波剌斯國，周數萬里。國大都城號蘇剌薩儻那，周四十餘里。川土既多，氣序亦異，大抵溫也。引水為田，人戶富饒。出金、鍮石、頗胝、水精、奇珍異寶，工織大錦、細褐、氍毺之類，多善馬、槖駝。貨用大銀錢。人性躁暴，俗無禮義。文字、語言異於諸國。無學藝，多工技，凡諸造作，隣境所重。婚姻雜亂，死多棄屍。其形偉大，齊髮露頭，衣皮褐，服錦㲲。戶課賦稅，人四銀錢。天祠甚多，提那跋外道之徒為所宗也。伽藍二三，僧徒數百，並學小乘教說一切有部法。釋迦佛鉢在此王宮。
translation: From here, going northwest, one reaches the country of Pārsa (波剌斯國) (although it is not a country of India, it is appended here as it lies along the route; the old name was Bosi (波斯), which is an abbreviation). The country of Pārsa is several tens of thousands of li in circumference. The great capital city of the country is named Sūlāsātǎngnà (蘇剌薩儻那), which is more than forty li in circumference. The land is vast and the climate is also distinct, being generally warm. Water is diverted to irrigate the fields, and the households are wealthy and prosperous. It produces gold, brass, quartz, crystal, and rare treasures and precious gems. The people are skilled at weaving large brocades, fine woolens, and rugs, and there are many fine horses and camels. For currency, they use large silver coins. The nature of the people is impetuous and violent, and their customs lack propriety and righteousness. Their script and language differ from those of other countries. They have no interest in academic arts but are skilled in crafts; all their manufactures are highly valued by neighboring regions. Marriages are promiscuous, and when people die, they are mostly abandoned as corpses. The people are large in stature, wear their hair cut level, and go bareheaded; they wear leather and wool garments and dress in brocade and felt. Regarding household taxes and levies, each person pays four silver coins. There are many deva temples, and the followers of the Dinaba (提那跋) heretics are those who revere them. There are two or three saṃghārāmas with several hundred monks, all of whom study the Hīnayāna teachings of the Sarvāstivāda school. The alms bowl of the Śākya Buddha is in the king’s palace here.

t2087_text: 自阿點婆翅羅國北行七百餘里，至臂多縶羅國（西印度境）。臂多縶羅國，周三千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛，無大君長，役屬信度國。土地沙鹵，寒風淒勁。多宿、麥，少花菓。而風俗獷暴。語異中印度。不好藝學，然知淳信。伽藍五十餘所，僧徒三千餘人，並學小乘正量部法。天祠二十餘所，並塗灰外道也。城北十五六里大林中，有窣堵波，高數百尺，無憂王所建也。中有舍利，時放光明。是如來昔作仙人，為國王所害之處。此東不遠有故伽藍，是昔大迦多延那大阿羅漢之所建立。其傍則有過去四佛座及經行遺迹之處，建窣堵波以為旌表。
translation: Traveling north from the country of Audumbatira (阿點婆翅羅國) for more than seven hundred *li*, one arrives at the country of Pi-to-zhi-luo (臂多縶羅國) (within the borders of Western India). The country of Pi-to-zhi-luo is more than three thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city is more than twenty *li* in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous; they have no great sovereign but are subject to the country of Sindhu (信度國). The land is sandy and saline, and the cold winds are biting. There is much winter wheat, but few flowers or fruits. The customs of the people are fierce and violent. Their language differs from that of Central India. They do not care for the arts or learning, yet they are sincere in their faith. There are more than fifty monasteries with over three thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Sāmmitīya school of the Lesser Vehicle. There are more than twenty *deva* temples, all belonging to the ash-smearing non-Buddhists. In a large forest fifteen or sixteen *li* north of the city, there is a *stūpa* several hundred feet high, built by King Aśoka. Inside it are relics that occasionally emit light. This is the place where the Tathāgata, in a former life as a *ṛṣi*, was harmed by a king. Not far to the east of this is an old monastery, which was established by the great arhat Mahākātyāyana. Beside it are the seats and walking paths of the four past Buddhas, where *stūpas* have been built to mark the sites.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 從此東北行三百餘里，至阿軬荼國（西印度境）。阿軬荼國，周二千四五百里。國大都城周二十餘里。無大君長，役屬信度國。土宜稼穡，宿、麥特豐，花菓少，草木疎。氣序風寒，人性獷烈。言辭朴質，不尚學業，然於三寶守心淳信。伽藍二十餘所，僧徒二千餘人，多學小乘正量部法。天祠五所，並塗灰外道也。城東北不遠，大竹林中，伽藍餘趾，是如來昔於此處聽諸苾芻著亟縛屣（唐言靴）。傍有窣堵波，無憂王所建也，基雖傾陷，尚高百餘尺。其傍精舍，有青石立佛像，每至齋日，或放神光。次南八百餘步，林中有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。如來昔日止此，夜寒，乃以三衣重覆，至明旦，開諸苾芻著複納衣。此林之中有佛經行之處。又有諸窣堵波，鱗次相望，並過去四佛坐處也。其窣堵波中有如來髮、爪，每至齋日，多放光明。
translation: From here, traveling northeast for more than three hundred li, one arrives at the country of Avaṇḍa (阿軬荼國) (in the region of West India). The country of Avaṇḍa is two thousand four or five hundred li in circuit. The capital city is over twenty li in circuit. There is no great monarch; it is subject to the country of Sindhu (信度國). The land is suitable for agriculture; winter wheat is especially abundant, while flowers and fruits are scarce, and trees and vegetation are sparse. The climate is windy and cold, and the nature of the people is fierce and impetuous. Their speech is simple and plain, and they do not value academic pursuits, yet they are pure and faithful in their devotion to the Three Jewels. There are over twenty saṃghārāmas with more than two thousand monks, most of whom study the teachings of the Hīnayāna Saṃmitīya school. There are five Deva temples, all belonging to the ash-smearing heretics. Not far to the northeast of the city, in a large bamboo grove, are the remaining foundations of a saṃghārāma; this is where the Tathāgata once permitted the bhikṣus to wear *jīvashī* (亟縛屣) (in Tang language: boots). Beside it is a stūpa built by King Aśoka; although the base has collapsed, it is still over one hundred feet high. In the *vihāra* (精舍) beside it, there is a standing Buddha image made of blue stone, which sometimes emits divine light on fast days. Eight hundred paces further south, in the forest, there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka. The Tathāgata once stayed here; because the night was cold, he covered himself with his three robes, and the next morning, he permitted the bhikṣus to wear quilted robes. In this forest, there is a place where the Buddha walked in meditation. There are also several stūpas, arranged like fish scales facing one another, which are the places where the four past Buddhas sat. Inside that stūpa are the hair and nail relics of the Tathāgata, which often emit divine light on fast days.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 從此東北行九百餘里，至伐剌拏國（西印度境）。伐剌拏國，周四千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛，役屬迦畢試國。地多山林，稼穡時播。氣序微寒，風俗獷烈。性急暴，志鄙弊。語言少同中印度。邪正兼崇，不好學藝。伽藍數十，荒圮已多，僧徒三百餘人，並學大乘法教。天祠五所，多塗灰外道也。城南不遠有故伽藍，如來在昔於此說法，示教利喜，開悟含生。其側有過去四佛座及經行遺迹之處。聞諸土俗曰：從此國西接稽畺那國，居大山間川，別立主，無大君長。多羊、馬，有善馬者，其形姝大，諸國希種，隣境所寶。復此西北，踰大山，涉廣川，歷小城邑，行二千餘里，出印度境，至漕矩吒國（亦謂漕利國）。
translation: From here, traveling northeast for more than nine hundred li, one reaches the country of Varaṇa (伐剌拏國) (in the territory of West India). The country of Varaṇa is over four thousand li in circuit. The capital city is more than twenty li in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous, and they are subject to the country of Kāpiśī (迦畢試國). The land has many mountains and forests, and crops are sown in their proper seasons. The climate is slightly cold, and the customs are fierce and violent. The people are impetuous and irritable, and their dispositions are base and corrupt. Their language is somewhat similar to that of Mid-India. They revere both heterodox and orthodox teachings, and they do not care for learning or the arts. There are several dozen monasteries, most of which are ruined and desolate; there are over three hundred monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Mahāyāna. There are five Deva temples, mostly belonging to the ash-smearing ascetics. Not far to the south of the city is an old monastery where the Tathāgata in the past preached the Dharma, manifesting teachings to bring benefit and joy, and enlightening living beings. Beside it are the seats of the four past Buddhas and the places where they walked in meditation. I have heard from the local people that to the west of this country, bordering the country of Jīmna (稽畺那國), the people live in the valleys among the great mountains; they have separate rulers and no great monarch. There are many sheep and horses. Those who possess good horses have animals that are large and beautiful in form; they are a rare breed among the various countries and are treasured by the neighboring regions. Traveling northwest from here again, crossing great mountains, traversing wide rivers, and passing through small towns and cities, one travels over two thousand li, leaves the borders of India, and reaches the country of Jāguḍa (漕矩吒國) (also called the country of Caoli (漕利國)).

t2087_text: 漕矩吒國，周七千餘里。國大都城號鶴悉那，周三十餘里，或都鶴薩羅城，城周三十餘里，並堅峻險固也。山川隱軫，疇壟爽塏。穀稼時播，宿麥滋豐，草木扶疎，花菓茂盛，宜欝金香，出興瞿草，草生羅摩印度川。鶴薩羅城中踊泉流派，國人利之，以溉田也。氣序寒烈，霜雪繁多。人性輕躁，情多詭詐。好學藝，多技術，聽而不明，日誦數萬言。文字言辭，異於諸國。多飾虛談，少成事實。雖祀百神，敬崇三寶。伽藍數百所，僧徒萬餘人，並皆習學大乘法教。今王淳信，累葉承統，務興勝福，敏而好學。無憂王所建窣堵波十餘所。天祠數十，異道雜居。計多外道，其徒極盛，宗事䅳（錫苟反，下同）那天。其天神昔自迦畢試國阿路猱山徙居此國南界䅳那呬羅山中，作威作福，為暴為惡，信求者遂願，輕蔑者招殃。故遠近宗仰，上下祗懼。隣國異俗君臣僚庶，每歲嘉辰不期而會，或齎金、銀、奇寶，或以牛、馬、馴畜，競興貢奉，俱伸誠素。所以金、銀布地，羊馬滿谷，無敢覬覦，唯修施奉。宗事外道，克心苦行，天神授其呪術，外道遵行多効，治療疾病，頗蒙痊愈。
translation: The country of Jaguḍa (漕矩吒國) is over seven thousand li in circuit. The great capital city of the country is called Ghasna (鶴悉那), which is over thirty li in circuit; sometimes the capital is at the city of Ghasala (鶴薩羅城), which is also over thirty li in circuit, and both are steep, rugged, and well-fortified. The mountains and rivers are undulating, and the fields and ridges are high and dry. Crops are sown in their proper seasons, winter wheat grows in abundance, vegetation is lush, and flowers and fruits are flourishing. The land is suitable for saffron (欝金香), and it produces the hingu herb (興瞿草), which grows in the Rāmēndu (羅摩印度) valley. In the city of Ghasala, there are gushing springs that flow in various directions, which the people of the country utilize to irrigate their fields. The climate is cold and harsh, with frequent frost and snow. The people are impulsive by nature and their dispositions are often deceitful. They are fond of learning arts and possess many technical skills; they listen but do not understand, yet they can recite tens of thousands of words a day. Their script and language differ from those of other countries. They often embellish empty talk and accomplish few practical results. Although they worship the hundred gods, they revere and honor the Three Jewels. There are several hundred monasteries and more than ten thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Mahāyāna. The present king is sincere in his faith, having inherited the throne through successive generations; he is devoted to performing meritorious deeds, and is intelligent and fond of learning. There are more than ten stūpas built by King Aśoka (無憂王). There are several dozen deva temples, where followers of different sects live together. Most of the people are non-Buddhists, and their disciples are extremely numerous; they worship the deity Śuna (䅳那) (䅳 is pronounced by the *fanqie* 錫苟, i.e. the initial of 錫 with the final of 苟; likewise below). This deity formerly moved from Mount Aruṇa (阿路猱山) in the country of Kāpiśī (迦畢試國) to reside in Mount Śunāśīra (䅳那呬羅山) on the southern border of this country, where he displays his power, bestows blessings, and commits acts of violence and evil; those who believe and pray to him have their wishes fulfilled, while those who despise him incur calamity. Thus, those far and near revere him, and those high and low stand in awe of him. The rulers, ministers, officials, and commoners of neighboring countries with different customs gather without appointment on auspicious days each year; they bring gold, silver, and rare treasures, or offer cattle, horses, and domestic animals, competing to present offerings to express their sincerity. Consequently, gold and silver are spread upon the ground and sheep and horses fill the valleys, yet no one dares to covet them, as all are intent only on making offerings. Those who follow non-Buddhist paths and practice asceticism with a disciplined heart are granted incantations by the celestial deity; the non-Buddhists who practice them find them highly effective, and those treated for illnesses are often healed.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal
translation_issues: note （錫苟反，下同） 'pronounced like si and gou, and so on below' → a fanqie: 䅳 is read with the initial of 錫 and the final of 苟; 'likewise below' (Beal: no note); Mount Aruṇa lacks its Chinese 阿路猱山

t2087_text: 從此北行五百餘里，至弗栗恃薩儻那國。弗栗恃薩儻那國，東西二千餘里，南北千餘里。國大都城號護苾那，周二十餘里。土宜風俗，同漕矩吒國，語言有異。氣序寒勁，人性獷烈。王，突厥種也，深信三寶，尚學遵德。
translation: From here, traveling northward for more than five hundred li, one arrives at the country of Vṛjiṣṭhāna (弗栗恃薩儻那國). The country of Vṛjiṣṭhāna is more than two thousand li from east to west and over one thousand li from north to south. The capital city of the country is named Hūbīnā (護苾那), and it is more than twenty li in circuit. The soil, products, and customs are the same as those of the country of Jaguḍa (漕矩吒國), though the language is different. The climate is cold and harsh, and the temperament of the people is fierce and impetuous. The king is of Turkic lineage; he has deep faith in the Three Jewels, values learning, and adheres to virtue.

t2087_text: 從此國東北，踰山涉川，越迦畢試國邊城小邑，凡數十所，至大雪山婆羅犀那大嶺。嶺極崇峻，危隥𢼨傾，蹊徑盤迂，巖岫回互。或入深谷，或上高崖，盛夏合凍，鑿氷而度。行經三日，方至嶺上。寒風凄烈，積雪彌谷，行旅經涉，莫能佇足。飛隼翱翔，不能越度，足趾步履，然後飜飛，下望諸山，若觀培塿。贍部洲中，斯嶺特高。其巔無樹，唯多石峯，攢立叢倚，森然若林。
translation: Proceeding northeast from this country, crossing mountains and fording rivers, and passing through several dozen small frontier towns of the country of Kāpiśī (迦畢試國), one reaches the Varasena (婆羅犀那) great range of the Great Snow Mountains. The range is extremely high and steep, with dangerous, precipitous slopes; the paths are winding and the cliffs and peaks interlock. Sometimes one enters deep valleys, and sometimes one ascends high precipices; even in the height of summer it is frozen over, and one must hack through the ice to cross. After traveling for three days, one finally reaches the top of the range. The cold wind is bitter and fierce, and accumulated snow fills the valleys; travelers passing through cannot find a place to stand. Soaring falcons cannot fly across it; they must walk on their feet before taking flight again. Looking down at the various mountains, they appear like small anthills. In the Jambudvīpa (贍部洲), this range is exceptionally high. Its summit has no trees, but only many stone peaks, clustered and leaning against one another, standing dense like a forest.

t2087_text: 又三日行，方得下嶺，至安呾羅縛國。安呾羅縛國，覩貨邏國故地。周三千餘里。國大都城周十四五里。無大君長，役屬突厥。山阜連屬，川田隘狹。氣序寒烈，風雪凄勁。豐稼穡，宜花菓。人性獷暴，俗無綱紀。不知罪福，不尚習學，唯修神祠，少信佛法。伽藍三所，僧徒數十，然皆遵習大眾部法。有一窣堵波，無憂王建也。
translation: After traveling for three more days, I finally descended from the mountain range and reached the country of Antarava (安呾羅縛國). The country of Antarava is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over three thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit. There is no great sovereign or leader, and it is subject to the Turks. The mountains and hills are connected, and the river valleys and fields are narrow and confined. The climate is cold and severe, and the wind and snow are biting and harsh. It is abundant in crops and suitable for flowers and fruits. The nature of the people is fierce and violent, and their customs lack order and discipline. They do not understand the concepts of sin or merit, and they do not value learning; they only maintain shrines to deities and have little faith in the Buddha-dharma. There are three monasteries with several dozen monks, all of whom follow the teachings of the Mahāsāṃghika school. There is one stūpa, which was built by King Aśoka.

t2087_text: 從此西北，入谷踰嶺，度諸小城，行四百餘里，至闊悉多國。闊悉多國，覩貨邏國故地也。周減千里。國大都城周十餘里。無大君長，役屬突厥。山多川狹，風而且寒。穀稼豐，花菓盛。人性獷暴，俗無法度。伽藍三所，僧徒尠少。
translation: From here, traveling northwest, entering valleys and crossing ridges, and passing through various small towns for over four hundred li, one reaches the country of Khost (闊悉多國). The country of Khost is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is less than one thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is over ten li in circuit. There is no great monarch, and it is subject to the Turks (突厥). The mountains are numerous and the rivers narrow; it is windy and cold. The grain crops are abundant, and flowers and fruits are plentiful. The nature of the people is fierce and violent, and their customs lack laws and regulations. There are three saṃghārāmas (伽藍), and the number of monks is very small.

t2087_text: 從此西北，踰山越谷，度諸城邑，行三百餘里，至活國。活國，覩貨邏國故地也。周二千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。無別君長，役屬突厥。上地平坦，穀稼時播，草木榮茂，花菓具繁。氣序和暢，風俗淳質。人性躁烈，衣服氈褐。多信三寶，少事諸神。伽藍十餘所，僧徒數百人，大小二乘，兼功綜習。其王，突厥也，管鐵門已南諸小國，遷徙鳥居，不常其邑。
translation: From here, going northwest across mountains and valleys and passing through various towns for over three hundred li, one arrives at the country of Huoh (活國). The country of Huoh is the ancient territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circuit. It has no separate ruler, being subject to the Turks (突厥). The land is level and flat; grain is sown in its season, vegetation is lush and flourishing, and flowers and fruits are abundant. The climate is mild and pleasant, and the customs are simple and honest. The people are impetuous and fierce by nature, and they wear garments of felt and coarse wool. They mostly believe in the Three Jewels and rarely worship other gods. There are more than ten monasteries and several hundred monks, who study both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings. Their king is a Turk who governs the various small countries south of the Iron Gate (鐵門); he moves about like a bird and has no permanent seat of government.

t2087_text: 從此東入葱嶺。葱嶺者，據贍部洲中，南接大雪山，北至熱海、千泉，西至活國，東至烏鎩國，東西南北各數千里。崖嶺數百重，幽谷險峻，恒積氷雪，寒風勁烈。多出葱，故謂葱嶺；又以山崖葱翠，遂以名焉。
translation: From here, traveling east, one enters the Congling (Onion Mountains). The Congling are situated in the center of Jambudvīpa; they connect to the Great Snow Mountains (大雪山) in the south, reach the Hot Sea (熱海) and the Thousand Springs (千泉) in the north, extend to the country of Huo (活國) in the west, and to the country of Wusha (烏鎩國) in the east. They extend for several thousand li in every direction. There are hundreds of layers of cliffs and ridges, with deep, precipitous valleys where ice and snow accumulate permanently and cold winds blow with great intensity. Because they produce many onions, they are called the Congling; furthermore, because the mountain cliffs are of an onion-green color, they are named accordingly.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

There is no great sovereign, and it is subject to the Turks.

The suitability of the soil and the customs are much the same as those of the country of Hu (活國).

To the north, it borders the Vaxšu River (縛芻河), and it is more than two hundred li in circuit. The capital city of the country is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit. The soil, products, and customs are much the same as those of the country of Hu (活國).

t2087_text: 從瞢健國東踰峻嶺，越洞谷，歷數川城，行三百餘里，至訖栗瑟摩國。訖栗瑟摩國，覩貨邏國故地也。東西十餘里，南北三百餘里。國大都城周十五六里。土宜風俗，大同瞢健國，但其人性暴愚惡有異。
translation: Going east from the country of Mungān (瞢健國), crossing steep mountain ranges, traversing deep valleys, and passing through several river cities for more than three hundred *li*, one reaches the country of Kṛṣma (訖栗瑟摩國). The country of Kṛṣma is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than ten *li* from east to west and three hundred *li* from north to south. The capital city of the country is fifteen or sixteen *li* in circumference. The native products and social customs are generally the same as those of the country of Mungān, but the people differ in being violent, foolish, and malicious in disposition.

It is over one hundred li from east to west and over three hundred li from south to north. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circumference. The soil, products, and customs are much the same as those of the country of Kṛṣma (訖栗瑟摩國).

t2087_text: 從訖栗瑟摩國東，踰山越川，行三百餘里，至呬摩呾羅國。呬摩呾羅國，覩貨邏國故地也。周三千餘里。山川邐迤，土地沃壤。宜穀稼，多宿麥，百卉滋茂，眾菓具繁。氣序寒烈，人性暴急，不識罪福，形貌鄙陋。舉措威儀，衣氈皮褐，頗同突厥。其婦人首冠木角，高三尺餘，前有兩岐，表夫父母；上岐表父，下岐表母，隨先喪亡，除去一岐，舅姑俱沒，角冠全棄。其先強國，王，釋種也，葱嶺之西，多見臣伏。境隣突厥，遂染其俗，又為侵掠，自守其境，故此國人，流離異域，數十堅城，各別立主，穹廬毳帳，遷徙往來。西接訖栗瑟摩國。
translation: Going east from the country of Kṛṣma (訖栗瑟摩國), crossing mountains and traversing rivers for over three hundred li, one reaches the country of Himatala (呬摩呾羅國). The country of Himatala is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over three thousand li in circumference. The mountains and rivers are winding and rugged, but the soil is fertile. It is suitable for grain crops, with an abundance of winter wheat; all kinds of plants grow luxuriantly, and various fruits are plentiful. The climate is cold and harsh. The people are violent and impetuous by nature, do not understand merit or sin, and their appearance is coarse and ugly. Their deportment and manners, as well as their clothing of felt and leather, are quite similar to those of the Turks. Their women wear wooden horns on their heads, over three feet high, with two branches in front representing their husband’s parents; the upper branch represents the father-in-law, and the lower branch represents the mother-in-law. As each passes away, the corresponding branch is removed; when both parents-in-law are deceased, the horn headdress is discarded entirely. In the past, this was a powerful kingdom, and the king was of the Śākya clan (釋種); to the west of the Onion Range (葱嶺), many states were subject to them. Because their borders neighbor the Turks, they have gradually adopted their customs; furthermore, due to being subjected to invasions and raids, they have had to defend their own territory. Consequently, the people of this country have been scattered into foreign lands, with dozens of fortified cities each having its own independent ruler, living in domed felt tents and moving about in search of pasture. To the west, it borders the country of Kṛṣma.

t2087_text: 東谷行二百餘里，至鉢鐸創那國。鉢鐸創那國，覩貨邏國故地也。周二千餘里。國大都城據山崖上，周六七里。山川邐迤，沙石彌漫。土宜菽、麥，多蒱陶、胡桃、梨、柰等菓。氣序寒烈，人性剛猛。俗無禮法，不知學藝。其貌鄙陋，多衣氈褐。伽藍三四所，僧徒寡少。王性淳質，深信三寶。
translation: Traveling east through the valley for more than two hundred *li*, one arrives at the country of Badakhshān (鉢鐸創那國). The country of Badakhshān is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than two thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city of the country is situated upon a mountain cliff and is six or seven *li* in circuit. The mountains and rivers are winding and rugged, and the land is filled with sand and stone. The soil is suitable for pulse and wheat, and there is an abundance of fruits such as grapes, walnuts, pears, and crabapples. The climate is cold and harsh, and the people are fierce and impetuous by nature. Their customs lack propriety and law, and they have no knowledge of the arts. Their appearance is coarse and ugly, and they mostly wear garments of felt and coarse wool. There are three or four *saṃghārāmas* (monasteries), with very few monks. The king is simple and honest by nature and has deep faith in the Three Jewels.

t2087_text: 從此東南，山谷中行二百餘里，至淫薄健國。淫薄健國，覩貨邏國故地也。周千餘里。國大都城周十餘里。山嶺連屬，川田隘狹。土地所產，氣序所宜，人性之差，同鉢鐸創那，但言語少異。王性苛暴，不明善惡。
translation: From here, traveling southeast through a mountain valley for more than two hundred li, one reaches the country of Yambagan (淫薄健國). The country of Yambagan is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than one thousand li in circumference. The capital city of the country is more than ten li in circumference. The mountain ranges are connected, and the river valleys and fields are narrow and confined. The native products, the climate, and the character of the people are the same as those of Badakshān (鉢鐸創那), though the language is slightly different. The king is harsh and violent by nature, and he does not distinguish between good and evil.

t2087_text: 從此東南，踰嶺越谷，峽路危險，行三百餘里，至屈（居勿反）浪拏國。屈浪拏國，覩貨邏國故地也。周二千餘里。土地山川，氣序時候，同淫薄健國。俗無法度，人性鄙暴。多不營福，少信佛法。其貌醜弊，多服氈褐。有山巖，中多出金精，琢析其石，然後得之。伽藍既少，僧徒亦寡。其王淳質，敬崇三寶。
translation: From here, traveling southeast, crossing ridges and traversing valleys along dangerous canyon paths for more than three hundred li, one reaches the country of Kuraṇa (屈浪拏國) (屈 is pronounced by the *fanqie* 居勿). The country of Kuraṇa is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than two thousand li in circumference. The land, topography, and climate are the same as those of the country of Yambagan (淫薄健國). The customs lack laws and regulations, and the people’s nature is base and violent. Most do not cultivate merit, and few believe in the Buddha-Dharma. Their appearance is ugly and wretched, and they mostly wear felt and coarse wool. There are rocky mountains that produce much gold essence; one must chisel and break the stones to obtain it. The monasteries are few, and the monks are also scarce. Their king is simple and sincere, and he reveres and honors the Three Jewels.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 從此東北，登山入谷，途路艱險，行五百餘里，至達摩悉鐵帝國（亦名鎮偘，又謂護蜜）。達摩悉鐵帝國，在兩山間，覩貨邏國故地也。東西千五六百餘里，南北廣四五里，狹則不踰一里。臨縛芻河，盤紆曲折，堆阜高下，沙石流漫，寒風淒烈。唯植麥、豆，少樹林，乏花菓。多出善馬，馬形雖小，而耐馳涉。俗無禮義，人性獷暴。形貌鄙陋，衣服氈褐。眼多碧綠，異於諸國。伽藍十餘所，僧徒寡少。
translation: From here, traveling northeast, climbing mountains and entering valleys along a difficult and dangerous path for over five hundred li, one arrives at the country of Dharmasthiti (達摩悉鐵帝國) (also called Zhenkan [鎮偘], and also called Humi [護蜜]). The country of Dharmasthiti lies between two mountains and is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over one thousand five or six hundred li from east to west, and four to five li wide from north to south, while at its narrowest it does not exceed one li. It borders the Vakṣu River (縛芻河), winding and twisting with uneven mounds and hillocks; sand and stones drift and spread, and the cold winds are harsh and piercing. They only plant wheat and beans; there are few forests and a lack of flowers and fruits. They produce many good horses; although the horses are small in stature, they are enduring in running and traveling. The customs lack propriety and righteousness, and the people’s nature is fierce and violent. Their appearance is base and ugly, and they wear felt and coarse wool garments. Their eyes are mostly emerald green, which is different from other countries. There are more than ten saṃghārāmas, but the number of monks is small.

t2087_text: 昏馱多城，國之都也。中有伽藍，此國先王之所建立，疏崖奠谷，式建堂宇。此國之先，未被佛教，但事邪神，數百年前，肇弘法化。初，此國王愛子嬰疾，徒究醫術，有加無瘳。王乃躬往天祠，禮請求救。時彼祠主為神下語：「必當痊復，良無他慮。」王聞喜慰，回駕而歸。路逢沙門，容止可觀，駭其形服，問所從至。此沙門者，已證聖果，欲弘佛法，故此儀形。而報王曰：「我，如來弟子，所謂苾芻也。」王既憂心，即先問曰：「我子嬰疾，生死未分。」沙門曰：「王先靈可起，愛子難濟。」王曰：「天神謂其不死，沙門言其當終，詭俗之人，言何可信？」遲至宮中，愛子已死。匿不發喪，更問神主，猶曰：「不死，疹疾當瘳。」王便發怒，縛神主而數曰：「汝曹群居長惡，妄行威福。我子已死，尚云當瘳，此而謬惑，孰不可忍？宜戮神主，殄滅靈廟。」於是殺神主，除神像，投縛芻河。迴駕而還，又遇沙門，見而敬悅，稽首謝曰：「曩無明導，佇足邪途，澆弊雖久，沿革在茲，願能垂顧，降臨居室。」沙門受請，隨至中宮。葬子既已，謂沙門曰：「人世糺紛，生死流轉，我子嬰疾，問其去留，神而妄言，當必痊差。先承指告，果無虛說，斯則其法可奉，唯垂哀愍，導此迷徒。」遂請沙門揆度伽藍，依其規矩，而便建立。自爾之後，佛教方隆。故伽藍中精舍，為羅漢建也。伽藍大精舍中有石佛像，像上懸金銅圓蓋，眾寶莊嚴。人有旋繞，蓋亦隨轉，人止蓋止，莫測靈鑒。聞諸耆舊曰：或云聖人願力所持，或謂機關祕術所致。觀其堂宇，石壁堅峻。考厥眾議，莫知實錄。
translation: The city of Khaṇḍata (昏馱多城) is the capital of the country. Within it is a monastery established by a former king of this country, who hollowed out the cliffs and filled the valleys to construct its halls and chambers. In earlier times, this country had not been reached by Buddhism and only worshipped heretical deities; it was only a few hundred years ago that the transformation of the Dharma began to spread.  Initially, the king’s beloved son fell ill. He exhausted all medical arts, but the illness only worsened without any sign of recovery. The king then went in person to a temple of the gods to offer rites and pray for salvation. At that time, the priest of the temple spoke on behalf of the deity: "He will certainly recover; there is truly no cause for concern." The king, hearing this, was joyful and comforted, and turned his carriage to return home. On the road, he encountered a śramaṇa whose demeanor was remarkable. Struck by his appearance and attire, the king asked where he had come from. This śramaṇa had already attained the holy fruit and, wishing to propagate the Buddha’s Dharma, had assumed this form. He replied to the king, "I am a disciple of the Tathāgata, what is known as a bhikṣu."  The king, being full of anxiety, immediately asked, "My son is afflicted with illness, and it is not yet certain whether he will live or die." The śramaṇa said, "The king’s ancestors may be raised, but your beloved son is difficult to save." The king said, "The heavenly deity said he would not die, yet this śramaṇa says he shall perish; how can the words of such a deceptive and vulgar man be trusted?"  Upon arriving at the palace, he found his beloved son had already died. He concealed the death and did not hold a funeral, instead asking the priest of the deity again, who still said, "He will not die; the illness will surely be cured." The king then flew into a rage, bound the priest, and rebuked him, saying, "You and your kind live together to foster evil, wantonly exercising power and claiming blessings." "My son is already dead, yet you still claim he will recover; such deceit and delusion are truly unbearable! It is fitting to execute the spirit-master and destroy the spirit-temple." Thereupon, he killed the spirit-master, removed the spirit-images, and cast them into the Vaxšu River (縛芻河). As he turned his carriage to return, he encountered a śramaṇa. Seeing him, he felt respect and joy, bowed his head, and apologized, saying, "In the past, I lacked a bright guide and lingered on evil paths. Although the corruption has lasted long, the reform begins here. I hope you will deign to look upon me and descend to my residence." The śramaṇa accepted the invitation and followed him to the inner palace. Once the son had been buried, the king said to the śramaṇa, "The human world is full of entanglement, and birth and death are in constant flux. When my son fell ill, I asked the spirit whether he would stay or depart, and the spirit spoke falsely, saying he would surely recover. Having previously received your instructions, which indeed proved not to be false, I see that your Dharma is worthy of devotion; I only pray that you will show compassion and guide this deluded follower." He then requested the śramaṇa to survey the site for a monastery (伽藍) and establish it according to the proper rules. From that time on, the Buddha's teaching flourished. Therefore, the vihāra (精舍) in the monastery was built for an arhat. In the great main hall of the monastery, there is a stone Buddha image, above which hangs a circular canopy of gilt bronze, adorned with various jewels. When people circumambulate, the canopy also rotates accordingly; when the people stop, the canopy stops. No one can fathom this spiritual manifestation. I heard from the elders that some say it is sustained by the power of a holy person's vow, while others say it is caused by secret mechanical arts. Observing the building, the stone walls are solid and steep. Examining all these opinions, no one knows the true account.

t2087_text: 踰此國大山，北至尸棄尼國。尸棄尼國，周二千餘里。國大都城周五六里。山川連屬，沙石遍野。多宿、麥，少穀稼，林樹稀疎，花菓寡少。氣序寒烈，風俗獷勇，忍於殺戮，務於盜竊，不知禮義，不識善惡。迷未來禍福，懼現世災殃。形貌鄙陋，皮褐為服。文字同覩貨羅國，語言有異。
translation: Crossing the great mountains of this country, one arrives north at the country of Šikni (尸棄尼國). The country of Šikni is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is five or six li in circuit. The mountains and rivers are connected, and the fields are covered with sand and stone. There is much winter wheat, but few cereal crops; trees are sparse, and flowers and fruits are scarce. The climate is bitterly cold. The customs of the people are fierce and brave; they are hardened to slaughter and devoted to theft. They do not know ritual or righteousness, and they do not distinguish between good and evil. They are confused about future misfortune or blessings, yet they fear the calamities of the present life. Their appearance is coarse and unsightly, and they wear skins and coarse wool for clothing. Their writing is the same as that of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨羅國), but their spoken language is different.

t2087_text: 越達摩悉鐵帝國大山之南，至商彌國。商彌國，周二千五六百里。山川相間，堆阜高下。穀稼備植，菽、麥彌豐，多蒱陶，出雌黃，鑿崖析石，然後得之。山神暴惡，屢為災害，祀祭後入，平吉往來。若不祈禱，風雹奮發。氣序寒，風俗急。人性淳質，俗無禮義，智謀寡狹，伎能淺薄。文字同覩貨邏國，語言別異。多衣氈褐。其王，釋種也，崇重佛法，國人從化，莫不淳信。伽藍二所，僧徒寡少。
translation: Crossing to the south of the great mountains of the country of Dharmasthiti (達摩悉鐵帝國), one arrives at the country of Śami (商彌國). The country of Śami is two thousand five or six hundred li in circumference. Mountains and rivers alternate, with high and low hills interspersed. All kinds of grain are planted, with pulse and wheat being particularly abundant; there are many grapes, and the land produces orpiment, which is obtained by splitting the rocks hewn from the cliffs. The mountain gods are fierce and malicious, repeatedly causing calamities; only after offering sacrifices can one enter, and then travel back and forth in safety. If one does not pray, winds and hail break out. The climate is cold, and the customs are impetuous. The people are simple and honest in disposition, but their customs lack etiquette and righteousness; their wisdom is limited, and their skills are superficial. Their script is the same as that of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國), but their spoken language is different. They mostly wear felt and coarse wool garments. Their king is of the Śākya clan and deeply reveres the Buddha's teachings; the people follow his example, and all are pure in their faith. There are two saṃghārāmas, with few monks.

t2087_text: 國境東北，踰山越谷，經危履險，行七百餘里，至波謎羅川。東西千餘里，南北百餘里，狹隘之處不踰十里。據兩雪山間，故寒風凄勁，春夏飛雪，晝夜飄風。地鹹鹵，多礫石，播植不滋，草木稀少，遂致空荒，絕無人止。
translation: To the northeast of the country, crossing mountains and traversing valleys, passing through dangerous terrain and treading over perilous paths for over seven hundred li, one arrives at the Pamir Valley (波謎羅川). It extends over one thousand li from east to west and over one hundred li from south to north, while at its narrowest point it is no more than ten li wide. It is situated between two snowy mountains, and therefore the cold winds are piercingly strong; snow falls during the spring and summer, and winds swirl day and night. The soil is saline and alkaline, with much gravel and stone; crops do not flourish, and vegetation is sparse, which leads to it being a desolate wilderness, entirely devoid of human habitation.

t2087_text: 波謎羅川中有大龍池，東西三百餘里，南北五十餘里，據大葱嶺內，當贍部洲中，其地最高也。水乃澄清皎鏡，莫測其深，色帶青黑，味甚甘美。潛居則鮫、螭、魚、龍、黿、鼉、龜、鼈，浮游乃鴛鴦、鴻雁、鴐鵝、鷫、鳵，諸鳥太卵，遺㲉荒野，或草澤間，或沙渚上。池西派一大流，西至達摩悉鐵帝國東界，與縛芻河合而西流，故此已右，水皆西流。池東派一大流，東北至佉沙國西界，與徙多河合而東流，故此已左，水皆東流。波謎羅川南越山，有鉢露羅國，多金、銀，金色如火。
translation: In the Pamir (波謎羅) Valley lies the Great Dragon Lake, extending over three hundred *li* from east to west and over fifty *li* from north to south. It is situated within the Great Onion Range (大葱嶺), lies at the center of Jambudvīpa (贍部洲), and occupies the highest elevation. The water is clear and bright as a mirror, its depth unfathomable, its color a dark blue-black, and its taste extremely sweet. Submerged within it dwell sharks, *chi*-dragons, fish, dragons, soft-shelled turtles, alligators, tortoises, and turtles. Floating and swimming upon it are mandarin ducks, wild geese, *jia*-geese, *su*-birds, and *hu*-birds. These birds lay large eggs, leaving their shells in the wilderness, either among the grassy marshes or upon the sandy islets. A large stream flows out from the west of the lake, running west to the eastern boundary of the Dharmasthiti (達摩悉鐵帝) country, where it joins the Vakṣu (縛芻) River and flows westward; therefore, to the right of this point, all waters flow to the west. A large stream flows out from the east of the lake, running northeast to the western boundary of the Khāsa (佉沙) country, where it joins the Sītā (徙多) River and flows eastward; therefore, to the left of this point, all waters flow to the east. South of the Pamir Valley, crossing the mountains, is the Balūra (鉢露羅) country, which abounds in gold and silver; the color of the gold is like fire.

t2087_text: 自此川中東南，登山履險，路無人里，唯多氷雪。行五百餘里，至朅盤陀國。朅盤陀國，周二千餘里。國大都城基大石嶺，背徙多河，周二十餘里。山嶺連屬，川原隘狹。穀稼儉少，菽、麥豐多，林樹稀，花菓少。原隰丘墟，城邑空曠。俗無禮義，人寡學藝。性既獷暴，力亦驍勇。容貌醜弊，衣服氈褐。文字、語言，大同佉沙國。然知淳信，敬崇佛法。伽藍十餘所，僧徒五百餘人，習學小乘教說一切有部。今王淳質，敬重三寶，儀容閑雅，篤志好學。建國已來，多歷年所。其自稱云是至那提婆瞿呾羅（唐言漢日天種）。此國之先，葱嶺中荒川也。昔波利剌斯國王娶婦漢土，迎歸至此，時屬兵亂，東西路絕，遂以王女置於孤峯，極危峻，梯崖而上下，設周衛警，晝巡夜。時經三月，寇賊方靜，欲趣歸路，女已有娠。使臣惶懼，謂徒屬曰：「王命迎婦，屬斯寇亂，野次荒川，朝不謀夕。吾王德感，妖氛已靜，今將歸國，王婦有娠。顧此為憂，不知死地，宜推首惡，或以後誅。」訊問諠譁，莫究其實。時彼侍兒謂使臣曰：「勿相尤也，乃神會耳。每日正中，有一丈夫從日輪中乘馬會此。」使臣曰：「若然者，何以雪罪？歸必見誅，留亦來討，進退若是，何所宜行？」僉曰：「斯事不細，誰就深誅？待罪境外，且推旦夕。」於是即石峯上築宮起館，周三百餘步。環宮築城，立女為主，建官垂憲。至期產男，容貌妍麗。母攝政事，子稱尊號。飛行虛空，控馭風雲，威德遐被，聲教遠洽，隣域異國，莫不稱臣。其王壽終，葬在此城東南百餘里大山巖石室中。其屍乾腊，今猶不壞，狀羸瘠人，儼然如睡，時易衣服，恒置香花。子孫奕世以迄于今。以其先祖之世，母則漢土之人，父乃日天之種，故其自稱漢日天種。然其王族，貌同中國，首飾方冠，身衣胡服。後嗣陵夷，見迫強國。無憂王命世，即其宮中建窣堵波。其王於後遷居宮東北隅，以其故宮，為尊者童受論師建僧伽藍，臺閣高廣，佛像威嚴。尊者，呾叉始羅國人也，幼而穎悟，早離俗塵，遊心典籍，棲神玄旨，日誦三萬二千言，兼書三萬二千字。故能學冠時彥，名高當世，立正法，摧邪見，高論清舉，無難不酬，五印度國咸見推高。其所製論凡數十部，並盛宣行，莫不翫習，即經部本師也。當此之時，東有馬鳴，南有提婆，西有龍猛，北有童受，號為四日照世。故此國王聞尊者盛德，興兵動眾，伐呾叉始羅國，脇而得之，建此伽藍，式昭瞻仰。
translation: From this valley, traveling southeast, one climbs mountains and traverses dangerous paths where there are no human habitations, only much ice and snow. After traveling more than five hundred li, one reaches the country of Kharbanda (朅盤陀國). The country of Kharbanda is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city is built upon a large rocky ridge, with the Sītā River (徙多河) at its back, and it is over twenty li in circuit. The mountain ranges are connected, and the valleys and plains are narrow. Grain crops are scarce, but beans and wheat are abundant; trees are sparse, and there is little fruit or flowers. The plains and marshes are desolate, and the cities and towns are empty. The customs lack propriety and righteousness, and the people have little learning or skill. Their nature is fierce and violent, yet they are also brave and valiant. Their appearance is ugly and wretched, and they wear garments of felt and coarse wool. Their script and language are largely the same as those of the country of Khāsa (佉沙國). However, they are sincere in their faith and deeply revere the Buddhadharma. There are more than ten monasteries and over five hundred monks, who study the teachings of the Small Vehicle (Hīnayāna) according to the Sarvāstivāda school. The current king is simple and honest, respects the Three Jewels, is refined and elegant in his demeanor, and is devoted to learning. Since the founding of the kingdom, many years have passed. The people claim to be the descendants of the *Cīna-deva-gotra* (至那提婆瞿呾羅) (in the language of the Tang, "the race of the Han and the Sun-deva"). The origin of this country was a desolate valley in the Onion Range (Pamirs). Long ago, a king of Persia (波利剌斯) married a princess from the land of Han and was escorting her back when they reached this place. At that time, there was a military rebellion, and the roads to the east and west were blocked. He therefore placed the princess upon an isolated peak, which was extremely steep and dangerous, accessible only by ladders to ascend or descend, and he stationed guards all around to keep watch day and night. Three months passed, and the bandits were finally pacified. When he intended to continue on the road home, the princess was already pregnant. The envoy was terrified and said to his retinue, "The King ordered us to welcome his bride, but we encountered this rebellion; camping in the wild barrens, we cannot even plan for the next morning. Through the virtue of our King, the baleful atmosphere has been cleared, and now we are to return to the kingdom, yet the King’s bride is pregnant. Considering this, we are in distress, not knowing where I shall die; we should seek out the chief culprit, so that he may be executed afterwards." There was a clamor of questioning, but no one could determine the truth. At that time, a maidservant said to the envoy, "Do not blame one another; it was a divine encounter. Every day at high noon, a man would arrive here on horseback, descending from the solar disc." The envoy said, "If that is the case, how can we clear ourselves of this guilt? If we return, we will surely be executed; if we stay, we will also be punished. With advancement or retreat being thus, what is the proper course of action?" They all agreed, "This matter is not trivial; who would willingly face such severe punishment? Let us await our fate outside the borders and delay for a while."  Thereupon, they built a palace and quarters on the stone peak, with a circumference of more than three hundred paces. They built a city wall around the palace, established the woman as sovereign, and instituted officials and laws. When the time came, she gave birth to a son, whose appearance was beautiful and refined. The mother managed the affairs of state, and the son assumed the royal title. He could fly through the void and control the wind and clouds; his majesty and virtue reached far and wide, and his reputation and teachings spread to distant lands. Neighboring regions and foreign countries all paid him homage. When the king died at a ripe old age, he was buried in a stone chamber within a large mountain over a hundred *li* southeast of this city. His corpse was preserved like a mummy and remains intact to this day; resembling an emaciated person, he looks as if he were fast asleep, and his clothes are changed periodically while incense and flowers are constantly placed before him. His descendants have continued through the generations down to the present day. Because in the time of their ancestor, the mother was a person from the land of Han (China) and the father was of the seed of the Sun God, they call themselves the "Han-Sun-God Clan." However, their royal family resembles the people of the Middle Kingdom (China) in appearance; they wear square crowns as head ornaments and dress in foreign clothing. Later, their descendants declined and were pressured by powerful states. King Aśoka (無憂王) appeared in the world and built a stupa within their palace. The king later moved his residence to the northeast corner of the palace and converted his former palace into a monastery for the venerable Shastra Master Kumāralāta (童受論師), with lofty, spacious terraces and pavilions and solemn, majestic Buddha statues. The venerable master was a native of the country of Takṣaśilā (呾叉始羅國); he was brilliant from childhood, renounced the secular world early, devoted his mind to the scriptures, and focused his spirit on the profound mysteries, daily reciting thirty-two thousand words and writing another thirty-two thousand. Thus, his learning surpassed the scholars of his time, and his fame was high in the world; he established the True Dharma, refuted heterodox views, and his lofty discourses were clear and elevated, leaving no difficulty unaddressed, so that he was universally esteemed throughout the five Indias. The treatises he authored number several dozen; they are all widely circulated and studied, for he is the founding master of the Sautrāntika school. At that time, there was Aśvaghoṣa in the east, Deva in the south, Nāgārjuna in the west, and Kumāralāta in the north; they were known as the "four suns that illuminate the world." Therefore, the king of this country, having heard of the venerable master's great virtue, mobilized his troops to attack the country of Takṣaśilā and obtained him by coercion; he then built this monastery to manifest his reverence.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

They built a city wall around the palace, established the woman as the ruler, and appointed officials to establish laws.

t2087_text: 城東南行三百餘里，至大石崖，有二石室，各一羅漢於中入滅盡定。端然而坐，難以動搖，形若羸人，膚骸不朽，已經七百餘歲，其鬚髮恒長，故眾僧年別為剃髮易衣。
translation: Traveling three hundred-odd *li* to the southeast of the city, one reaches a great rocky cliff where there are two stone chambers, in each of which an Arhat (阿羅漢) has entered the samādhi of extinction (滅盡定). They sit upright and are difficult to move; their forms resemble those of emaciated men, yet their skin and bones have not decayed, having already remained so for over seven hundred years. Their hair and beards grow constantly, and for this reason, the monks shave them and change their robes every year.

mz_identification: SE of Tashkurghan, perhaps Kandar Punin mountain (following 白鳥)

t2087_text: 大崖東北，踰嶺履險，行二百餘里，至奔（通論反）穰舍羅（唐言福舍）。葱嶺東岡，四山之中，地方百餘頃，正中墊下。冬夏積雪，風寒飄勁。疇壟舃鹵，稼穡不滋，既無林樹，唯有細草。時雖暑熱，而多風雪，人徒纔入，雲霧已興，商侶往來，苦斯艱險。聞諸耆舊曰：昔有賈客，其徒萬餘，槖駝數千，齎貨逐利，遭風遇雪，人畜俱喪。時朅盤陀國有大羅漢，遙觀見之，愍其危厄，欲運神通，拯斯淪溺；適來至此，商人已喪。於是收諸珍寶，集其所有，構立館舍，儲積資財，買地隣國，鬻戶邊城，以賑往來。故今行人商侶，咸蒙周給。
translation: To the northeast of the great cliff, crossing ridges and traversing dangerous paths for over two hundred *li*, one arrives at Puṇyaśālā (奔穰舍羅) (奔 is pronounced by the *fanqie* 通論; in the Tang language, "House of Merit"). It is situated on the eastern ridge of the Onion Range (葱嶺), amidst four mountains, in a basin over one hundred *qing* in area, sunken in the center. Snow accumulates there throughout winter and summer, and the wind is cold and fierce. The fields and ridges are saline and barren, so crops do not grow; there are no trees, only fine grass. Even during the heat of summer, there is much wind and snow; as soon as travelers enter, clouds and mist arise, and merchant caravans suffer greatly from these hardships and dangers.  I have heard from the elders: once there were merchants with a following of over ten thousand and several thousand camels, carrying goods in pursuit of profit, who encountered wind and snow, and both people and animals perished. At that time, there was a great Arhat in the kingdom of *Kharbanda* (朅盤陀國) who saw them from afar; pitying their peril, he desired to exercise his supernatural powers to rescue them from their plight, but by the time he arrived, the merchants had already perished. He then collected their various treasures, gathered all that remained, constructed a building, stored up provisions, purchased land in neighboring countries, and bought households in border cities to provide relief for those traveling to and fro. Therefore, travelers and merchant caravans today all receive support from this.
translation_source: DharmaMitra, corrected against Mizutani and Beal

t2087_text: 從此東下葱嶺東岡，登危嶺，越洞谷，谿徑險阻，風雪相繼，行八百餘里，出葱嶺，至烏鎩國。烏鎩國，周千餘里。國大都城周十餘里，南臨徙多河。地土沃壤，稼穡殷盛，林樹欝茂，花菓具繁。多出雜玉，則有白玉、黳玉、青玉。氣序和，風雨順。俗寡禮義，人性剛獷，多詭詐，少廉恥。文字、語言少同佉沙國。容貌醜弊，衣服皮褐。然能崇信敬奉佛法。伽藍十餘所，僧徒減千人，習學小乘教說一切有部。自數百年，王族絕嗣，無別君長，役屬朅盤陀國。
translation: From this point, going eastward down the eastern ridges of the Pamir Mountains (葱嶺), climbing perilous peaks and crossing deep valleys, through dangerous mountain paths and amid continuous wind and snow, I traveled over eight hundred li, emerged from the Pamirs, and reached the kingdom of Wusha (烏鎩國). The kingdom of Wusha is over one thousand li in circuit. The capital city is over ten li in circuit and borders the Sītā River (徙多河) to the south. The soil is rich and fertile, crops are abundant, forests are lush, and flowers and fruits are plentiful. The land produces much variegated jade, including white jade, black jade, and green jade. The climate is temperate, and the wind and rain are timely. The customs lack propriety and righteousness; the people are by nature stubborn and fierce, prone to deceit, and lacking in shame. Their writing and language are somewhat similar to those of the kingdom of Khāsa (佉沙國). Their appearance is unsightly, and they wear garments of leather and wool. Nevertheless, they are able to revere and serve the Buddhadharma. There are more than ten saṃghārāmas, with fewer than one thousand monks, who study the teachings of the Small Vehicle according to the Sarvāstivāda school. For several hundred years, the royal line has been extinct, and having no separate ruler, they are subject to the kingdom of Kharbanda (朅盤陀國).
